Perimeter & Network Security: Manage enterprise firewall policies, site-to-site and remote access VPN tunnels, IPS/IDS, URL filtering, log shipping to SIEM, and incident triage. Modern Endpoint Management: Oversee the full lifecycle of employee workstations—from imaging, provisioning, and patch deployment to endpoint compliance tracking and asset inventory. Threat Mitigation & Compliance: Administer EDR/XDR security agents, isolate endpoint threats, enforce IT security SOPs, and ensure audit readiness for data protection standards. Operational Excellence & Vendor Management: Drive L1/L2 incident resolution, maintain exhaustive system architecture diagrams and SOPs, and manage IT vendor contracts, warranty claims, and escalations. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR? Experience: 4–7 years of hands-on experience in enterprise systems administration, network engineering, or infrastructure support. Systems & Directory Services: Deep expertise in Windows Server (2016/2019/2022), Active Directory design/maintenance, Group Policy (GPO), and enterprise backup and disaster recovery tools. Core Networking: Strong grasp of TCP/IP networking, subnetting, VLAN segmentation, routing/switching fundamentals, and wireless infrastructure (WLAN). Firewall & Security Administration: Proven track record configuring and auditing enterprise firewalls (e.g., Fortinet, Palo Alto, Sophos), site-to-site IPsec/SSL VPNs, and endpoint protection suites (EDR/XDR). Endpoint & Productivity Suites: Practical administration of Microsoft 365 / Entra ID (Azure AD), automated software deployment tools, and disk imaging systems. NICE-TO-HAVES: Relevant industry certifications: CCNA, Microsoft Certified: Windows Server Hybrid Administrator Associate, CompTIA Security+, or vendor firewall certifications (e.g., NSE 4). Experience administering virtualized environments (VMware vSphere / Microsoft Hyper-V). Prior experience supporting high-security manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or hardware engineering facilities. Exposure to SIEM log ingestion, centralized syslog servers, or network monitoring tools (PRTG, Zabbix, Nagios).
